correction.text: Bulgaria within its post-1940 borders, 110,018 km2: the shape unchanged, but its years run 1946-1947 and it belongs to the People's Republic from 15 September 1946, not to the Kingdom

keyframe_review.note: Years and owner change, the outline stays. Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Bulgaria' row has one shape, dated 1947, but the Kingdom page gives 'Monarchy abolished: 15 September 1946' (infobox) and 'The republic was formally proclaimed a week later' after the plebiscite of September 1946 (95.6 percent for a republic, People's Republic page), so a 1947 shape cannot belong to the Kingdom: it is the People's Republic's territory, and 1946 from September has no other shape of record. The Kingdom itself (Tsardom, 5 October 1908 to 15 September 1946) is drawn by the principality-of-bulgaria dossier, so no dossier of its own is kept for it. The outline is the interwar one plus Southern Dobruja ('On 7 September 1940 Bulgaria succeeded in negotiating the recovery of Southern Dobruja', Kingdom page; the peace settlement left Bulgaria 'allowed to keep Southern Dobruja', People's Republic page, and 'restored to its borders of 1 January 1941', Paris treaties page). Area 110,018 km2 against the Kingdom infobox's 122,134 km2 for 1915 (ratio 0.90; the page does not say which borders that figure counts, so the 10 percent is not read as a shape fault) and the People's Republic infobox's 110,994 km2 (no year; ratio 0.99).

109,612 km2 against the infobox's 110,994 km2 (no year; ratio 0.99). One cell (about 250 km2) near Blagoevgrad differs from the 1947 shape, which is drawing noise: the page says 'Geographically, the People's Republic of Bulgaria had the same borders as present-day Bulgaria.' It also says Pirin Macedonia became part of federal Yugoslavia under 1947 agreements with Yugoslavia, which contradicts that sentence and the shape, which keeps Blagoevgrad; not applied (notes).

109,564 km2 for 1949-1989 (ratio 0.99): the same land, no border change; the Dimitrov Constitution of December 1947, the Zhivkov Constitution of 18 May 1971 and the fall of Zhivkov on 10 November 1989 move no line.
Same outline as 1949 (109,564 km2); the country is renamed the Republic of Bulgaria on 15 November 1990 and Cliopatria's Republic row has the identical outline from 1991.

ledger.note: 1946: the monarchy is abolished and the People's Republic follows. 'In September 1946, the monarchy was abolished by plebiscite, which resulted in 95.6 percent voting in favour of a republic'; infobox 'Monarchy abolished: 15 September 1946'; the Kingdom page: 'The republic was formally proclaimed a week later.' The pages give the date, not a frontier.

region.text: the whole country, which keeps its outline as the Republic of Bulgaria

ledger.note: 1990: the People's Republic ends. 'On 15 November 1990, the seventh Grand National Assembly voted to change the country's name' to the Republic of Bulgaria (infobox 'End of the People's Republic: 15 November 1990').

certainty.note: Treaty frontiers: Southern Dobruja kept and the 1 January 1941 borders restored by the 1947 peace treaty; the page says the republic 'had the same borders as present-day Bulgaria'.

notes: Same state as the Tsardom drawn by principality-of-bulgaria (that dossier ends on 15 September 1946 and names this state as successor); Wikidata Q121932 is shared with republic-of-bulgaria (1991-2024), which is the same land renamed on 15 November 1990 and keeps its own dossier (another part of eu-22; it founds from this state), so the two are not merged. Cliopatria dates this row 1948-1990 and its 'Kingdom of Bulgaria' row 1947; the keyframe kingdom-of-bulgaria_1947 here (years 1946-1947, verdict adjust) is that Kingdom row's single shape. 1946 overlaps the principality dossier's 1946 keyframe for the months before 15 September. No territorial event after 1946: the 1947 Paris treaty (effective 15 September 1947) confirmed Southern Dobruja and the borders of 1 January 1941, which the principality dossier records as the 1940 Craiova gain. The People's Republic page also says Pirin Macedonia 'became part of federal Yugoslavia' under 1947 agreements with Yugoslavia; no other page opened says so, the page's own sentence on borders and Cliopatria's shape (Blagoevgrad kept) contradict it, so it is not applied; a gap-filler could open 'Pirin Macedonia' or 'Bled agreement'. The Allied Control Commission, Soviet troops in Bulgaria to 1947 and the armistice of 28 October 1944 are not on the pages opened. Rulers are the infobox's party or government leaders (de facto leaders), not heads of state. Gazetteer names: none missing. REPAIR PASS 2026-11-01: the reviewer failed the sibling dossier kingdom-of-bulgaria (an alias for the Tsardom that principality-of-bulgaria already carries, with a duplicate 1908 found, a duplicate 1940 Southern Dobruja gain against Romania's single loss, and a duplicate 1946 dissolve) and this dossier took over its only Cliopatria row: 'Kingdom of Bulgaria' (Q147909, one shape, 1947) is now in cliopatria_names, its shape is reviewed here as kingdom-of-bulgaria_1947 (adjust, 1946-1947, same outline), and kingdom-of-bulgaria is dropped from the predecessors. kingdom-of-bulgaria.json is withdrawn (deleted); the colour agent needs no hue for that slug, and if the orchestrator requires a file for every Cliopatria slug it must rule on an alias form, since the schema has none. Not on the pages opened for the Kingdom: the 8 September 1946 plebiscite date, the armistice of 28 October 1944, the Paris treaty text. Disagreement with the reviewer: none.
